title: Key transit routes
steps: International gateway: fly into and out of Tokyo (HND/NRT). Neither Fukuoka nor Sapporo has scheduled nonstop US service in this trip's window — Fukuoka's international terminal is genuinely dense but skews toward Seoul/Asia (~182 weekly FUK↔ICN flights across 8 carriers), and Sapporo's first-ever North America nonstops (United from SFO, Air Canada from YVR) don't start until Dec 2026, just after this trip ends. A Tokyo connection on both ends is the realistic plan — a same-day domestic connection after a ~13-hr flight is possible but tight; an overnight near the airport is the gentler option and matches the trip's slow pace.
Tokyo → Fukuoka (start of trip): frequent domestic route, ANA/JAL/budget carriers, ≈2 hrs. Land at Fukuoka Airport (FUK) — genuinely close-in, ~15 min subway to Hakata Station.

Fukuoka regional rail: the JR Kyushu Northern Kyushu Area Pass (5-day, ¥17,000 — jrkyushu.co.jp, confirmed direct 2026-07-29) covers Fukuoka/Nagasaki/Saga/Oita/Kumamoto — worth it only if day trips actually range that far; for a Fukuoka-city-based stretch (Tenjin/Hakata/Nakasu/Dazaifu), point-to-point IC-card fares are likely cheaper. Dazaifu is a direct ~30-min Nishitetsu train from Fukuoka (Tenjin) Station.

Fukuoka → Sapporo (direct flight): ≈2h10–2h20, JAL mainline plus Peach/Jetstar/Skymark budget carriers — this direct link is what makes Hokkaido and Fukuoka work as adjacent legs without detouring through Tokyo. Land at New Chitose Airport (CTS), ≈40 min JR rapid airport train to Sapporo Station.

Sapporo regional: Otaru is a ≈35-min JR rapid-train ride from Sapporo Station. Noboribetsu is ≈1h15 by JR Limited Express Hokuto, or a direct reserved bus from New Chitose. Jozankei is ≈60 min via the direct Jotetsu Bus 'Kappa Liner' from Sapporo Station, or ≈75 min on the regular Jotetsu Bus #7/#8 (cheaper). The JR East–South Hokkaido Rail Pass (6 consecutive days, ¥40,000) bundles this region with Tohoku (see below) — only worth it if the specific 6 travel days line up; otherwise pay per-ride.

Sapporo → Sendai (direct flight): ≈1h10–1h20, JAL/ANA — the Hokkaido Shinkansen still doesn't reach Sapporo (extension now delayed to FY2038), so this is a straightforward case of fly-don't-overland; the rail alternative would be a 6–7 hr multi-transfer slog through Tokyo. Land at Sendai Airport, ≈25 min JR/rail-transfer or direct airport line into Sendai Station.

Sendai regional: Matsushima is ≈40 min on the JR Senseki Line — get off at Matsushimakaigan Station specifically, not 'Matsushima Station' (which is well away from the bay). Naruko Onsen/Gorge is ≈90 min via Tohoku Shinkansen to Furukawa then the JR Rikuu East Line, or ≈2 hrs direct on the Tohoku Main Line + Rikuu East Line. Zao Onsen is reached via the JR Senzan Line to Yamagata (≈70–90 min) plus a local bus (≈35–40 min), or — if it's running outside peak ski season, worth confirming — a more direct highway bus from Sendai Station (≈1h25).

Sendai → Tokyo → international departure (end of trip): Tohoku Shinkansen 'Hayabusa,' ≈90 min, all-reserved, ≈¥11,410 one-way standard reserved seat. Connect to HND/NRT for the international flight home.

Luggage forwarding (Yamato Ta-Q-Bin): genuinely useful for this itinerary — ask any hotel front desk for 'takkyubin,' ≈¥1,600–3,700 (≈$11–25) per suitcase. Standard transit is next-day, not same-day — ship a day ahead of when you need bags at the destination, and confirm with the receiving hotel that they'll accept an early delivery. Best uses on this trip: sending the big suitcases ahead before the Zao Onsen overnight (travel light to the ryokan with just an overnight bag), and again before the final Sendai→Tokyo leg.

title: Scenic rail — the honest picture
body:
The intake asked for scenic routes over the fastest option where the schedule allows — worth being upfront that the two most obvious answers here have both effectively expired. The Furano-Biei Norokko train (Hokkaido's classic autumn scenic run) ends its 28-year run for good on Sept 28, 2026, before this trip even starts. Its Tohoku equivalent, the old 'Resort Minori' observation train, retired back in 2020. Its direct successor, the rapid 'Yukemuri' train (Sendai↔Naruko Onsen↔Shinjo via the Rikuu East Line, ≈¥530 reserved-seat surcharge only), ran a dedicated autumn-color special in 2025 on weekends and holidays, Oct 18–Nov 16 — a genuinely nice window, except this itinerary's free Tohoku days (Nov 2–5) are all weekdays, since the following weekend is committed to the Sendai anchor event. So this guide plans around the regular, non-special Rikuu East Line local instead — same route, same window views, ordinary rolling stock, no reserved-seat surcharge. If Yukemuri's exact 2026 dates (published by JR East Tohoku ~Aug/Sept) end up falling on a free day, treat riding it as a nice upgrade, not a plan requirement.

For Hokkaido, the honest substitute is the regular (no reservation, no special name) JR Hakodate Main Line between Otaru and Yoichi — genuine coastal/cliff scenery, runs year-round on ordinary local trains, no seasonal expiry risk.
